ateret-zekenim/1:_: After reading the megillah etc. — Maharil wrote: after they prayed Maariv they wait until night and read the megillah; and see above siman 687 whether one may read before night — Minhagim wrote; and one does not say Lamenatzeach and not E-lo E-lo in the two days of Purim; and likewise in the name of Tosafot that one does not say Lamenatzeach; Kol Bo wrote; and one does not say Mizmor L'todah. We are not accustomed thus and say Mizmor L'todah. Our custom is to read the megillah and Asher He'enia and say Vayehi Noam and make havdalah and say V'titen Lecha — and so in Minhagim.
baer-heitev/1:ב: Vayehi Noam. After reading the megillah — Minhagim; and likewise Mahari Abuhav who wrote that they say Vayehi Noam — to exclude Kol Bo who ruled one does not say it at all; and what he wrote "and they read the megillah" refers after it, and afterward they make havdalah; and see in Shoneh Halachot in Hagahot Beit Yosef letter 4; and see in responsum Devar Shmuel siman 128.
baer-heitev/3:_: Lamenatzeach. Bach wrote in the name of Tosafot Megillah daf 4 that they say the song Mizmor L'Asaf which contains a fall for idolaters.
beer-hagolah/1:א: Tur in the name of R' Yehuda.
beer-hagolah/1:ב: There — and he explains: as on other days of the year after the order of Kedushah etc.; and it came only to inform us that we delay havdalah after megillah reading because we take out the day first.
beer-hagolah/3:ב: Tur in the name of a responsum he found; and likewise Orach Chayyim.
beur-hagra/1:א: Seif 1 — one says VeAtah Kadosh. Because it is adjacent after the verse Elohai Ekra etc., and the entire psalm is said about Esther as Rashi wrote 4:1; Kol Bo and Hagahot Maimoniot and Mordekhai.
beur-hagra/4:ג: When there is a word etc. — as the Taz wrote 2; and sheshon — this is a word etc. And it requires study: even communal work we delay, and its time is morning — kal vachomer a word which is only because of alacrity etc.; and likewise Peri Chadash.
biur-halacha/4:_: They take out a Torah scroll etc. — Tosafot Megillah (daf 4) wrote that one does not return the Torah scroll to its place but sits holding it until they finish reading the megillah; and in Levush it implies he returns the Torah scroll to its place and then reads the megillah; and likewise in Darkhei Moshe; afterward I found in Beit Meir who wrote: most poskim omitted Tosafot's words — implying they do not hold thus; and it appears the reason is that the holder too must intend to fulfill hearing megillah reading as stated siman 690 s.k. 14; and if he holds a Torah scroll his heart should be on the Torah scroll as stated siman 96 regarding prayer — end of his words.
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Magen Avraham beginning of the siman — view of Minhagim. NB it requires study: above siman 500 s.k. 59 he wrote Rama in name of Minhagim: all Kaddishim said after Eichah do not say Titkabel; and if you would say after megillah of Eichah they do not say Titkabel — then there is no Kaddish here that should have Titkabel except Shacharit, since that of Maariv they already said before Eichah; and what does "all the Kaddishim" mean — rather certainly after megillah of Eichah one should say Titkabel, if not because of Tisha B'Av "You have heard my prayer" — and so on Purim it would be fit to say it after megillah reading; but in truth we have only custom; and so fit to attach Titkabel to Maariv prayer as much as possible; but Magen Avraham's words always require study. Again I found in Hagahot Asheri end of Masechet Taanit like our custom — see there; requires study.
chokhmat-shlomo/2:_: Seif 2 in the gloss: one does not say on the miracles except on day 14 but not on 15 etc. NB see Taz s.k. 3; and see proof in Rashi chapter 2 of Shabbat s.v. lo mazkerinan who explained they were not obligated to mention; and afterward s.v. eino mazkir — need not mention. From this it implies: even per the view that it was not enacted to mention in Birkat Hamazon — nevertheless if he mentioned it is not an interruption; and he may also mention l'chatchila. And it is proven: anything connected to these days' event is not this interruption; and so on 15 as well — understand and check.
kaf-hachayyim/4:_: (ד) There — one says VeAtah Kadosh. The reason — Kol Bo wrote siman 45: because megillah reading is by day and night, a verse emerged as written Ekra yomam velo ta'aneh velailah velo dumiah li; and this verse is in the psalm Eli Eli lamah azavtani said about Esther; therefore they are accustomed to open after reading with VeAtah Kadosh which is in that psalm. Shulchan Gavoah letter 2.
levushei-serad/2:_: s.k. 2 — and his words: days that do not have etc. that do not have Musaf — if he did not say on the miracles in Chanukah and Purim they do not return him — so in Yerushalmi; and further our version there: he erred and did not mention Rosh Chodesh in Birkat Hamazon — they do not return him since it is possible without eating bread; this would say on Rosh Chodesh; but Shabbat and Yom Tov, Chanukah and Purim which cannot be without bread — they return. And it appears to Rabbenu Yonah: even though he mentions here that Chanukah mention is optional in Birkat Hamazon — since all are accustomed to mention and he also blessed intending to mention — we treat it as obligatory to mention — end Mordekhai.
levushei-serad/3:_: There — and from his custom thus, clearly. Meaning: he did not erase Purim — implying he holds on Purim the beginning and end are true in Birkat Hamazon stricter than prayer.
levushei-serad/4:_: There the word veChanukah etc. — for otherwise he would not have mentioned Chanukah law in Birkat Hamazon at all.
machatzit-hashekel/1:_: Magen Avraham wrote in Minhagim etc.; and likewise Maharshal in name of Rokeach etc.; in Agudah wrote in name of Rokeach etc.; if so there are two witnesses contradicting each other in Rokeach's words.
machatzit-hashekel/2:א: (s.k. 2) One does not read etc. still servants of Achashverosh. Meaning: in Mordechai's days when the miracle occurred it was impossible for them to say servants of the Name, for they were still servants of Achashverosh; if so we too do not say Hallel.
magen-avraham/2:_: Written in Minhagim that they say full Kaddish after Maariv prayer before megillah reading; and likewise Maharil in responsum siman 56 Rokeach; and likewise Tosafot daf 4 and Hagahot Maimoniot unlike Levush; and in Agudah wrote in name of Rokeach to say half-Kaddish; and in Masechet Taanit wrote regarding Tisha B'Av they say Shema before Eichah; but Rokeach wrote to say half-Kaddish — end; and Abudraham also wrote half-Kaddish. It appears to me: in these countries where they say full Kaddish, then after megillah reading they say Shema without Titkabel; and possible this is Minhagim's view — siman 559; but not on 15. However if they said it they do not return him as written s.k. 108 unlike Bach.
magen-avraham/3:_: One does not read Hallel in it. For on Exodus we say Hallelu avdei HaMakom velo avdei Pharaoh; but here we are still servants of Achashverosh. In the morning they rise early to synagogue and do not don tefillin until after megillah reading [Matteh Moshe — Minhagim].
mishnah-berurah/3:א: (ז) Hallel — for on Exodus we say Hallelu avdei HaMakom velo avdei Pharaoh; but here we are still servants of Achashverosh.
mishnah-berurah/3:ב: (ח) And one does not fall etc. — and one does not say Lamenatzeach etc. on the two days of Purim because it is written therein tzarah vetzarah — on Purim we do not mention it.
mishnah-berurah/4:ג: (יא) And they read the megillah — and bless afterward Harav et riveinu as above siman 692; and all must hear the blessing; and some of the masses say Kaddish then after finishing the megillah — and this is not correct.
peri-megadim/2:_: And if I copy Taz — I will copy Mordekhai chapter Bameh Madlikin — see Shabbat 24a: days without Musaf — Semag ruled: if he did not say on miracles in Chanukah and Purim they do not return him; and so in Tosefta and Yerushalmi; and days without Musaf such as Chanukah and Purim — if they did not say they do not return him; and further our version there: he erred and did not mention Rosh Chodesh in Birkat Hamazon — they do not return him since possible without bread; this would say Rosh Chodesh; but not Shabbat and Yom Tov and Chanukah and Purim which cannot be without bread — they return; and it appears to Rabbenu Yonah: even though he mentions here Chanukah mention is optional in Birkat Hamazon — since all are accustomed to mention and he blessed intending to mention — we treat it obligatory — end Mordekhai Krakow edition. And it appears his words contradict: first he wrote on Chanukah and Purim they do not return, then he wrote they return; and some erase at the end Chanukah and Purim only Shabbat and Yom Tov; and Mahari Pollak erased the word Chanukah but Purim in prayer they do not return and in the meal they return. Taz challenged from "and it appears to Rabbenu Yonah" etc. — requires study; Taz's conclusion: on the first morning meal of 14 they return in Birkat Hamazon; but night of 14 after megillah or second meal on day 13 they do not return. Chemed Moshe wrote Tur in 687 wrote Chanukah and Purim need not return — perhaps there second meal and after megillah at night; and in 682 Chanukah he wrote explicitly prayer and Birkat Hamazon they do not return; here 693 Tur wrote Purim in prayer they do not return and in Birkat Hamazon — unclear whether meal requiring bread; and here 695 they return because bread is required; Magen Avraham 695 letter 9 they do not return. If so Taz has a new dispute: meal requiring bread — Magen Avraham fulfills with fruit and meat — requires study; will explain further in 695.
shaarei-teshuvah/2:_: Vayehi Noam. And see Be'er HaGolah; and see there in Devar Shmuel who wrote most of the world are accustomed to precede megillah reading to havdalah on the cup in synagogue — meaning also after finishing order of Kedushah and Kaddish Titkabel as custom all year; but since there is no ruling from Talmud and rishonim one should not compel a community to change custom; each community is a city unto itself; and this is not lo titgodedu etc.; and see in Maharshal Yoreh Deah siman 170; and see Magen Avraham siman 693; and see Eliyah Rabbah that Peri Chadash wrote one should make havdalah before — not fit to benefit from the candle before havdalah — end; and per this it suffices if he blesses Borei Meorei HaEsh; and Beit Din was perplexed how to discharge his wife with this blessing etc.; if so he should bless meein sheva in synagogue before havdalah since many rabbanan wrote to bless meein sheva first so as not to benefit without blessing etc.; and see in Shoneh Halachot in name of Maharash Halevi he need not bless meein sheva first since they order afterward on the cup and candle benefit was already discharged in Yotzer HaMeorot and it is only remembrance of what happened to Adam — see there; and see Tosefta Pesachim daf 91; and see Shiryei Shoneh Halachot: even on Tisha B'Av night they bless before — there he will not order on the cup that night etc.; one who blessed meein sheva before megillah did not lose — see there. Shaarei Chaim brought from Torat Chesed also Shoneh Halachot in name of Maharash Halevi etc. and my words above — see there. Regarding moving megillah on Shabbat to bring to synagogue mibaal yad for Purim night on Motzei Shabbat — see above siman 688 on 15 falling on Shabbat where Peri Chadash wrote forbidden to move; and in Shoneh Halachot siman 308 somewhat doubts; Shaarei Chaim brought in name of Matteh Yehudah: even for Peri Chadash prohibition only if falls on 15 since reading obligation exists; but other Shabbatot Rabba's decree does not apply — why forbid reading like Torah reading; and since reading permitted, carrying permitted; and Shoneh Halachot seems to lean thus; and world custom is lenient — end; and see above siman 308 in my words I brought from Eliyah Rabbah megillah law is like ketavim kodesh and Peri Chadash forbids; per Matteh Yehudah one can say they do not argue — Eliyah Rabbah other Shabbatot of the year and Peri Chadash agrees; but bringing to synagogue before night I would prevent because of preparation from Shabbat to weekday as explained siman 696. Now we found thus in omissions end of Moed Katan — see there. One may be strict not to bring via a minor — see responsa Beit Ephraim Yoreh Deah siman 62 and 63; rather wait until dark or bring discreetly mibaal yad to synagogue and study it somewhat as learning — then it does not look so much like preparation; and see Magen Avraham siman 334 s.k. 18 regarding megillah not written properly — nevertheless we save etc. — see there.
shaarei-teshuvah/3:_: (Seif 3 in Shulchan Aruch) one does not read Hallel in it. Eliyah Rabbah wrote in name of Meiri: for this reason they said in Berachot because its reading is hallelah — if he has no megillah to read he should say Hallel etc.; and Eliyah Rabbah wrote: since Rava said the reason is we are still servants of Achashverosh etc. — he should not say Hallel at all; and halacha is like Rava who is later; and also per Rif, Rosh, and Ran Rava challenges etc. — implies halacha is like him since they did not answer him; therefore poskim ruled he never says Hallel — see there; but in Mishna Berurah he brought Beit Yosef and Rambam also wrote reading is hallelah as Meiri implies and gives R' Nachman's reason etc. — see there; and per this the law returns: one without megillah says Hallel; but in my view the Talmud's main intent is the core enactment; but after they did not enact Hallel on Purim because reading is hallelah — automatically no place to read Hallel what Chazal did not enact for that day; and in my view nevertheless when he has no megillah he may read Hallel without blessing before and after like reading Tehillim — and this is fine; and even if he has a chumash and reads megillah for himself — one who wants also to read Hallel without blessing did not lose; possible saying Hallel they did not enact is better with some kedusha like a Torah scroll unlike megillah reading whose core enactment is to be written properly — therefore he fulfills both.
shaarei-teshuvah/4:_: (Seif 4 in Shulchan Aruch) they take out a Torah scroll etc. — see in Shulchan Aruch ch. 1 siman 9: a townsman who went to a city intending to return at megillah reading time — his day 15 when he is not obligated on 14; and he prays in synagogue with the congregation and may receive aliyah in parashat Vayavo Amalek even though today he has no megillah reading obligation; and see there regarding fast day when kohen does not fast he leaves synagogue; and regarding ben Eretz Yisrael who intends to return regarding reading in chutz la'aretz on second day Yom Tov — Shulchan Aruch; and I wrote from this in Shaarei Ephraim — see there.
turei-zahav/2:_: If they did not say etc. — Mordekhai siman 200 wrote: days without etc. — it became obligatory on him etc. — end; and his words contradict regarding Chanukah and Purim: first he said they do not return, at end wrote they return — besides opposing Talmud in explaining they do not return; many great ones erase the words on Chanukah and Purim at the end; and Rashal in responsum siman 48 wrote a great one of his generation Mahari Pollak erased veChanukah at the end; and from his custom thus — both are true: Purim evening and morning they do not return him — not better than prayer; but Purim meal which prophets and sages imposed on all Israel as days of feasting and joy more than Shabbatot and Yom Tov etc. — if so not less than Shabbat meal etc. — end; found his conclusion: on Purim there is a distinction — they return only in Purim meal, not evening and morning and Minchah — not in prayer nor Birkat Hamazon except meal time alone. I question this gloss from what Mordekhai wrote in name of Rabbenu Yonah etc. — even though he concludes here Chanukah mention is optional in Birkat Hamazon etc. — implies Yerushalmi had veChanukah; and all the more the first gloss I mentioned that they erased veChanukah and Purim entirely; and in my humble opinion the opposite is in Mordekhai regarding Chanukah — and so it should read: this would say Rosh Chodesh and Chanukah but not Shabbat Yom Tov and Purim which cannot be without eating etc. — Purim has obligation like Shabbat and Yom Tov as written yemei mishteh vesimchah; and Rava said Purim meal eaten at night did not fulfill — implying the meal is obligatory; if so certainly one must eat; and Tur's view seems thus who wrote in 695 they say on miracles in Hodah and did not mention if they did not say they do not return as in 682 Chanukah — rather certainly as he explained; and so for halacha as Rashal in name of Mahari Pollak: in Birkat Hamazon of the meal one must return for on miracles in Purim; but it seems not specifically meal after Minchah but first meal one eats on Purim — for the core reason is meal obligation that day as yemei mishteh vesimchah and insufficient without eating; if so first meal eaten that day fulfills Purim meal thereby; and we need not hang the law on what we call meal after Minchah Purim meal which is added joy — and on this insufficient without eating — so for practical halacha.
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Magen Avraham to say Chatzi Kaddish etc.; and in Rokeach before us explained siman 311; also regarding Tisha B'Av only after kinot one says without Titkabel but before they complete; also Agudah on megillah in name of Rokeach is unclear — see there Rokeach siman 244; and for our custom where they say Shema — it appears even if Purim falls on Motzei Shabbat they also say Shema after prayer; and so Eliyah Rabbah — see there; and so Maharil.
